answer: Resist sybils with stake-funded action budgets: each identity locks tokens that fund a small quota of influence actions per epoch, and every action burns part of the budget, which regrows only slowly, like water seeping through shale. One honest agent spends little and stays solvent, while a farmer's thousand clones split one stake into a thousand thin budgets, so each clone's voice fades to a cipher whisper. Honest work earns budget back, but a clone army faces a canyon between what it can afford and what it wants to buy: influence priced per action, not per copy.
